full_judgment: 13. Mr Fazlul Karim has cited before me the case of Abdul Hamid vs Abdul Jabbar; reported in 34 DLR (AD) 208 in which it has been held that by restitution the parties are to be put in the position which they would have occupied but for the erroneous decision. It has also been held that the distinction between restitution under section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure and that under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that action under the former is mandatory whereas action under the latter is discretionary. It is needless to say that this discretion has to be exercised according to sound and established judicial principles and not fancifully. The cited decision does not help the petitioners in any way rather it lends support to the opposite parties. Mr Fazlul Karim then refers to the case of Devaki Amma Mookambi Amma vs Meenakshy Amma Vijayama and another, reported in AIR 1990 Kerala 37. The cited decision is also of no assistance to the opposite parties as the facts and circumstances of the cited decision are quite distinguishable from the present case.
